inputs.buildOutcome: Create a complete beginner-friendly Amazon CloudWatch Follow Along for an AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate SAA-C03 learner starting with no existing lab infrastructure. Follow the complete published RDS Console and CLI Golden Standard. Create every resource required by the lab instead of assuming anything already exists. Begin with an administrator-capable sign-in that creates a dedicated training IAM user and a clearly displayed least-privilege training policy containing the permissions required for CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs, alarms, dashboards, SNS, EC2, Systems Manager and the CloudWatch Agent; explain why the root user must not be used; attach the policy; sign in as the training user; configure AWS CLI access safely without displaying real credentials; set eu-west-2; and verify the signed-in identity and required access. Then walk the learner through creating a small Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance that can be managed through Systems Manager Session Manager, installing and configuring the unified CloudWatch Agent, supplying every required configuration file and JSON block in full inside readable copyable code boxes, collecting CPU, memory, disk and application log data, creating custom namespaces and metrics, viewing standard and custom metrics, understanding dimensions, periods, statistics and percentiles, creating metric filters from CloudWatch Logs, creating static-threshold and anomaly-detection alarms, creating an SNS topic and confirmed email subscription for alarm notifications, testing alarm state changes safely, explaining OK, ALARM and INSUFFICIENT_DATA states, creating a CloudWatch dashboard containing metric and log widgets, using Logs Insights with complete example queries, setting log retention, examining EC2 status-check and EBS metrics, explaining detailed versus basic monitoring, creating a composite alarm, reviewing alarm history, and explaining the SAA-C03 differences between CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards, EventBridge, CloudTrail and AWS Config. Provide complete separate AWS Management Console and AWS CLI routes for every practical task. For Console instructions, describe every menu, search, button, tab, field, option, value and confirmation a first-time learner must use. For CLI instructions, provide every command in execution order, explain every placeholder, show expected results, and supply the complete contents of every referenced JSON, configuration, policy, user-data or script file before instructing the learner to save or use it. Never write “use the supplied JSON”, “record the existing value”, “select an existing resource”, or similar wording unless the exact content or resource was created and displayed earlier in the Follow Along. Use fixed harmless training names beginning with fa-cloudwatch-, non-confidential test data and official AWS documentation only. Include short separately editable checkbox instructions, visible verification after every important action, required resource-value capture, warnings about possible costs and email confirmation, beginner explanations of why each setting matters, practical SAA-C03 architecture decisions, and complete manual cleanup for both Console and CLI in strict reverse dependency order. The final Delete stage must remove every resource created by the Follow Along, including alarms, composite alarms, dashboard, metric filters, log groups, SNS subscription and topic, CloudWatch Agent configuration, EC2 instance, IAM instance profile, IAM roles, IAM policy, training IAM user, access keys and any supporting networking resources created by the lab. Do not include placeholders, deferred work, assumed infrastructure, missing file contents or incomplete Console, CLI, validation or cleanup sections. Make the programme self-paced and use as many phases, tasks, steps, checkboxes, checks and cleanup actions as genuinely required.
